question: What is a veth pair, and how does it give a container in its own network namespace a way to talk to the host?
answer_hinglish:
veth pair ek virtual Ethernet cable hai: kernel do interfaces banata hai jo hamesha jode mein aate hain. Ek end mein packet bhejo, woh doosre end se nikalta hai. Network namespace ka matlab hai container ka apna alag network stack: apne interfaces, apne routes, apni iptables. Naya namespace bilkul khaali hota hai -- sirf lo, aur woh bhi down.

Toh container ko bahar se jodne ka simplest tareeka: veth pair banao, ek end host ke namespace mein rakho, doosra container ke namespace mein. Dono ends par ek hi chhote subnet ke addresses do, link up karo -- ab host aur container ek doosre ko ping kar sakte hain.

minibox mein `--net veth` exactly yeh karta hai: host end ka naam `mbx` + 8 hex (jaise mbx1a2b3c4d) aur address 10.200.N.1/30; container end `eth0` aur 10.200.N.2/30. /30 mein sirf 2 usable addresses hote hain, toh har container ka apna point-to-point link hai. Docker ka default network bhi yahi se shuru hota hai, phir woh host ends ko ek bridge (docker0) mein lagata hai aur NAT add karta hai -- minibox wahan ruk jaata hai (stage 4b nahi kiya). Default ab bhi `--net none` hai: sirf loopback.
why_needed: Container networking ki har cheez (bridge, NAT, port publishing) veth ke upar banti hai; isko samjhe bina docker network samajh nahi aata.
real_world_analogy: Do kamron ke beech deewar mein ek pipe: ek taraf se baat karo, doosri taraf sunai deta hai. Bridge baad mein aata hai jab bahut saare kamre ek hall se jodne ho.
how_it_works: veth driver har transmit ko seedha peer ke receive path par daal deta hai (koi physical wire nahi). Dono ends alag namespaces mein ho sakte hain; ek end delete karo toh dono delete. Address add karne par kernel connected route khud banata hai (10.200.N.0/30 dev eth0).
in_this_project: minibox/network.py mein VethLink(host_if, subnet) host_ip = subnet[1], container_ip = subnet[2] deta hai. Test test_eth0_has_the_container_address_and_only_a_connected_route asli kernel par check karta hai ki eth0 par woh address hai, link UP hai, aur sirf ek route hai.
advantages: Simple: koi bridge ya iptables nahi
Har container ka alag /30, toh containers ek doosre se alag
disadvantages: Internet access nahi (NAT nahi)
Har container ke liye ek /30 = 4 addresses kharch
common_mistakes: Sochna ki naya network namespace host ka network share karta hai
Interface ko address dena par up karna bhool jaana
Dono ends ek hi namespace mein bana dena
follow_up_questions: veth aur tap device mein kya fark hai?
Bridge ke saath /30 ki jagah /24 kyun use hota hai?
Ek end delete karne par doosre ka kya hota hai?

question: How does minibox create the veth pair so that the container end is born inside the container's network namespace, without running `ip`?
answer_hinglish:
minibox `ip` command nahi chalata; woh wahi karta hai jo `ip link add` andar karta hai: NETLINK_ROUTE socket par ek RTM_NEWLINK message bhejta hai (stdlib `socket.AF_NETLINK`).

Message ka structure: nlmsghdr (16 bytes), phir ifinfomsg (host end, index 0 = naya banao), phir attributes: IFLA_IFNAME = 'mbx...' aur IFLA_LINKINFO. LINKINFO ke andar IFLA_INFO_KIND = 'veth' aur IFLA_INFO_DATA; DATA ke andar VETH_INFO_PEER, aur PEER ke andar peer ka apna poora ifinfomsg + IFLA_IFNAME = 'eth0' + IFLA_NET_NS_PID = INIT ka PID. Yeh aakhri attribute kernel ko bolta hai: peer ko us process ke network namespace mein banao.

Fayda: eth0 kabhi host par exist hi nahi karta, toh koi moment nahi jab half-configured interface host par pada ho, aur baad mein 'move to namespace' ka alag step nahi. Flags NLM_F_CREATE | NLM_F_EXCL hain (naam pehle se ho toh EEXIST), aur NLM_F_ACK se kernel ka jawab aata hai; negative error OSError(errno) ban jaata hai.

Mutation N8 ne IFLA_NET_NS_PID hata diya: peer HOST namespace mein 'eth0' naam se bana, container mein eth0 mila hi nahi, 12 tests red. Runner ne har baar check kiya ki host par koi stray eth0 nahi bacha.
why_needed: Container runtimes (runc, CNI plugins) yahi netlink calls karte hain; samajhna zaroori hai ki 'ip' sirf ek client hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko sirf parcel nahi, delivery address bhi dena: 'yeh doosra dibba seedha padosi ke ghar pahunchao'. Pehle apne ghar mangwa kar phir le jaane ki zaroorat nahi.
how_it_works: Kernel veth_newlink peer ke attributes alag se parse karta hai (rtnl_link_get_net se namespace resolve), peer ko us net mein register karta hai, phir host end ko current namespace mein. PID host ke PID namespace ka hona chahiye -- host process init_pid wahi dekhta hai.
in_this_project: rtnetlink.veth_body() pure function hai, unit test use parse karke nested structure check karta hai; asli check A2 par kernel ka accept karna hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/rtnetlink.py
def veth_body(name: str, peer: str, peer_netns_pid: int) -> bytes:
    peer_part = (IFINFOMSG.pack(socket.AF_UNSPEC, 0, 0, 0, 0)
                 + attr_str(IFLA_IFNAME, check_ifname(peer))
                 + attr_u32(IFLA_NET_NS_PID, peer_netns_pid))
    linkinfo = attr(IFLA_INFO_KIND, b"veth") + attr(IFLA_INFO_DATA, attr(VETH_INFO_PEER, peer_part))
    return (IFINFOMSG.pack(socket.AF_UNSPEC, 0, 0, 0, 0)
            + attr_str(IFLA_IFNAME, check_ifname(name))
            + attr(IFLA_LINKINFO, linkinfo))
disadvantages: Byte layout khud sambhalna padta hai
Kernel ke error messages (extack) parse nahi kiye
common_mistakes: Peer ko host mein banakar baad mein move karna (beech mein race)
PID container ke andar wala (1) bhejna, host wala nahi
NLM_F_EXCL na lagana aur kisi existing interface ko chhoo dena
follow_up_questions: IFLA_NET_NS_PID ki jagah IFLA_NET_NS_FD kab use karoge?
Kernel extack (NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG) kaise padhoge?
Interface naam 15 bytes tak hi kyun?

question: Explain the netlink message format (nlmsghdr, family header, rtattr) and why 4-byte padding matters.
answer_hinglish:
Netlink ek datagram protocol hai user space aur kernel ke beech. Har message: nlmsghdr = len (u32, poora message), type (u16, jaise RTM_NEWLINK = 16), flags (u16: REQUEST, ACK, CREATE, EXCL, DUMP), seq (u32, jawab match karne ke liye), pid (u32, 0 = kernel). Uske baad family header: links ke liye ifinfomsg (16 bytes: family, type, index, flags, change), addresses ke liye ifaddrmsg (8 bytes: family, prefixlen, flags, scope, index).

Phir attributes (rtattr): 2-byte length, 2-byte type, payload. Length field mein padding SHAMIL NAHI hoti, lekin agla attribute hamesha 4-byte boundary par shuru hota hai. Example: IFLA_IFNAME 'eth0\0' = 4 header + 5 = length 9, phir 3 zero bytes padding, total 12. Attributes nest hote hain: payload khud attributes ki list ho sakta hai (LINKINFO -> INFO_DATA -> VETH_INFO_PEER).

Padding kyun matter karta hai: kernel agla attribute NLA_ALIGN(len) ke baad dhoondhta hai. Padding hata do toh 'eth0\0' ke baad agla attribute galat offset par padhega. Mutation N10 ne yahi kiya: 13 tests red (unit test ke hand-written bytes bhi, aur A2 par kernel ne requests reject kiye). Type ke upar ke 2 bits flags hain (NESTED, NET_BYTEORDER), isliye parser 0x3FFF mask lagata hai.
why_needed: Netlink Linux networking ka control plane hai: ip, iw, NetworkManager, CNI sab isi se baat karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Courier ke dabbe: har dabbe par label (size + kya hai), aur dabbe hamesha 4 ke multiple wale shelf slots mein rakhe jaate hain. Agar ek dabba aadha slot le aur agla turant shuru ho, toh padhne wala galat label padhega.
how_it_works: Kernel nlmsg_parse / nla_parse attributes ko policy ke against validate karta hai (jaise IFLA_IFNAME string, max 15 + NUL). Reply ACK ek NLMSG_ERROR message hai jisme error 0 ya -errno, aur original request ka header.
in_this_project: minibox/rtnetlink.py mein attr(), message(), parse_attrs(), parse_messages() pure functions hain. tests/unit/test_rtnetlink.py expected bytes haath se likhta hai (kernel headers se), encoder se nahi banata.
advantages: Extensible: naye attributes purane clients ko nahi todte
Nesting se complex config ek message mein
disadvantages: Binary format, galti silent ho sakti hai
Host byte order (=) -- network order nahi
common_mistakes: Length field mein padding jod dena
Network byte order (!) use karna
Reply ko seq se match na karna
follow_up_questions: Dump response multipart kaise khatam hota hai?
NLA_F_NESTED flag kab zaroori hai?
Reply buffer chhota ho toh kya hota hai (MSG_TRUNC)?

question: The host and INIT live in different namespaces but must take turns to set up the network. How does minibox order these steps, and what breaks if the host does not wait?
answer_hinglish:
Problem: veth ka peer INIT ke network namespace mein banana hai, lekin woh namespace tab tak exist nahi karta jab tak INIT unshare(CLONE_NEWNET) na kare. Aur INIT ko eth0 configure karna hai, lekin woh tab tak nahi ho sakta jab tak host ne pair na banaya ho. Do processes, do namespaces, ek strict order.

minibox do pipes use karta hai. to_init (host -> INIT): pehla byte 'x' = tum cgroup mein ho; phir ek line = tumhara /30. from_init (INIT -> host): byte 'n' = mera network namespace ban gaya. Order: (1) host INIT ko cgroup mein daalta hai, 'x' likhta hai; (2) INIT unshare karta hai, lo up, 'n' likhta hai; (3) host 'n' ka wait karta hai -- EOF matlab INIT mar gaya, setup fail 125 -- phir lock ke andar /30 chunta hai, pair banata hai (peer = INIT ka PID), apna end configure karta hai, net.json likhta hai, /30 bhejta hai; (4) INIT eth0 configure karta hai, phir mounts, pivot_root, exec.

Agar host wait na kare (mutation N11): host IFLA_NET_NS_PID = INIT ka PID bhejta hai jab INIT abhi HOST ke namespace mein hai, toh 'eth0' host par ban jaata hai -- 3 tests red. Yeh classic race hai: 'PID ka namespace' ek moving target hai. Read ka result bhi check hota hai (b'n' na mile toh error), kyunki EOF ko success samajhna hi woh bug hai jo stage 1 ke cgroup pipe mein README ne honestly likha hai (INIT wahan byte check nahi karta).
why_needed: Multi-process setup mein 'kaun pehle' galat hua toh bugs sirf kabhi-kabhi dikhte hain; explicit handshake hi ilaaj hai.
real_world_analogy: Do log ek deewar ke aar-paar pipe fit kar rahe hain: ek bolta hai 'maine chhed kar diya', tabhi doosra pipe daalta hai, phir woh bolta hai 'pipe aa gaya', tab pehla apni taraf se kasta hai.
how_it_works: Pipe read blocking hai, toh wait ke liye koi sleep ya polling nahi. Writer ka end band ho toh read EOF (b'') deta hai -- yahi failure detection hai. Pipe fds CMD ko inherit nahi hone chahiye: INIT exec se pehle to_init_r band karta hai.
in_this_project: container.run() aur setup_container() dono taraf ka code hai; tests mein N11 ise pakadta hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py (host side, trimmed)
        os.write(to_init_w, b"x")
        if cfg.network == "veth":
            from . import network
            os.close(from_init_w)
            if os.read(from_init_r, 1) != b"n":     # EOF: INIT died before unsharing its network
                raise RuntimeError("container exited before its network namespace was ready")
            os.close(from_init_r)
            link = network.setup_host_side(init_pid)
            with open(os.path.join(state, "net.json"), "w") as f:
                json.dump(link.as_dict(), f, indent=1, sort_keys=True)
            os.write(to_init_w, f"{link.subnet}\n".encode())
        os.close(to_init_w)
advantages: INIT ko setns ki zaroorat nahi
disadvantages: Do pipes aur fds ka hisaab rakhna padta hai
Host SIGKILL ho jaaye toh uska pipe end band, INIT ko EOF milta hai aur woh 125 se exit karta hai -- lekin agar host end ban chuka tha toh woh leak hota hai (koi cleanup nahi chala)
common_mistakes: Sleep se order banana
Read ka result check na karna (EOF = success maan lena)
Setup pipe ko CMD mein leak kar dena
follow_up_questions: Host setns() se khud eth0 configure kare toh kya trade-off hai?
Pipe ki jagah socketpair ya eventfd kab?
Host SIGKILL ho jaaye toh INIT kahan atakta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: INIT apna half khud karta hai (address, up) -- host ko setns nahi karna padta, aur host process kabhi container namespace mein nahi jaata. Cost: INIT mein netlink code chalta hai aur do pipes.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Host wait skip kare: peer host par ban jaata hai (N11). INIT unshare se pehle mare: host ko EOF, setup 125, cleanup chalta hai. Host pair banane ke baad fail: setup_host_side apna end delete karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: runc jaisa: runtime namespace banata hai, CNI plugin setns karke configure karta hai. Ya pehle network namespace ko bind-mount karke naam do (ip netns), phir process ko usme bhejo.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har container ek round-trip handshake + kuch netlink calls -- milliseconds. Bottleneck lock hai (allocation serialize), jo IPAM ko central banane par jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Handshake ke har step par timeout; INIT ka cgroup byte bhi check karna; network setup ko ek plugin interface (CNI jaisa) ke peeche rakhna.

question: How does minibox pick a free /30 for each container, and why does it need a file lock? How was the race proven?
answer_hinglish:
Allocation simple hai: host ke saare IPv4 addresses netlink dump (RTM_GETADDR, NLM_F_DUMP) se lo, phir 10.200.0.0/16 ke /30 subnets mein se pehla chuno jo kisi existing network se OVERLAP na kare. Overlap check (sirf exact address nahi) ka matlab: agar host khud 10.0.0.0/8 mein ho, toh poora pool overlap karta hai, minibox refuse karta hai -- warna ek route host ke asli network ka hissa chhupa deta.

Race: yeh 'check-then-act' hai. Container A addresses padhta hai, B bhi padhta hai, dono ko 10.200.0.0/30 free dikhta hai, dono apne host end par 10.200.0.1 laga dete hain (Linux alag interfaces par same address allow karta hai) -- do containers ek hi subnet par, routing toot jaati hai.

Ilaaj: /run/minibox-net.lock par fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX), 'addresses list' se 'host end ko address mil gaya' tak. Lock ke andar kaam milliseconds ka hai. Lock file state_dir mein nahi, fixed path par hai, kyunki alag state dirs wale containers bhi same host network share karte hain.

Proof: pehle mutation N7 (lock hata do) pakda nahi gaya -- tests sequential the. Phir test_parallel_starts_get_distinct_subnets add kiya jo 8 containers ek saath start karta hai aur check karta hai ki 8 alag subnets mile; bina lock ke 3 mein se 3 runs red. Lesson: concurrency guard ka test tabhi hai jab test sach mein concurrency paida kare.
why_needed: IPAM (IP address management) har container platform ka core hai; check-then-act races wahan sabse common bug hain.
real_world_analogy: Parking lot mein do log ek saath khaali spot dekhte hain aur dono gaadi ghusa dete hain. Gate par ek token system (lock) chahiye: token lo, spot chuno, gaadi lagao, token wapas.
how_it_works: flock advisory lock hai: sirf woh processes respect karte hain jo bhi flock lete hain. Process mar jaaye toh kernel lock khud chhod deta hai (fd band). Lock file khud tmpfs par khaali file hai.
in_this_project: network.pick_subnet() pure function hai (unit tests: free, skip used, wider host net, pool full, refuse). _allocation_lock() context manager hai; setup_host_side ise ipv4_addresses() se add_address() tak pakadta hai.
advantages: Kernel hi source of truth (koi stale state file nahi)
Crash safe: lock process ke saath chhoot jaata hai
disadvantages: Har start par poora address dump (O(addresses))
Sirf ek host ke andar; multi-host IPAM nahi
Lock file /run mein reh jaati hai
common_mistakes: State file mein 'next index' rakhna (crash ke baad stale)
Sirf exact address check, overlap nahi
Race ke liye sequential test likhna
follow_up_questions: Lock file ko delete karna race kyun hai?
Multi-host par IPAM kaise karoge?
Routes bhi check karne chahiye ya sirf addresses?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Kernel state se allocation (stateless) vs ek IPAM database (fast, multi-host, lekin consistency ka jhanjhat). Single host ke liye kernel dump + lock sabse simple sahi solution.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Lock nahi: duplicate subnets (N7). Overlap check nahi: host ke used ranges par container (N6, 6 failed). Pool full: RuntimeError, setup 125.
advanced.alternatives: CNI host-local IPAM: /var/lib/cni/networks mein per-IP files + lock. Docker: libnetwork ka in-memory allocator, daemon ke andar.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 16384 /30 ka pool; lekin dump har start par -- 1000s containers ke saath bridge + /24 (ek address per container) behtar.
advanced.production_improvements: Allocation ka record (container name -> subnet) rakhna for inspect/gc; pool configurable; routes bhi overlap check mein.

question: The kernel deletes a veth pair when its namespace dies. Why does minibox still delete the host end explicitly, and how was that proven to matter?
answer_hinglish:
Sach hai: ek end jis namespace mein hai woh namespace destroy ho toh kernel pair delete kar deta hai, aur ek end delete karna doosra bhi delete karta hai. Toh pehli nazar mein cleanup ki zaroorat nahi lagti -- aur pehle test mein mutation N5 (explicit delete hatao) pakda bhi nahi gaya: normal exit ke baad link chala gaya tha.

Lekin namespace tab marta hai jab USKO koi refer na kare. Process ke alawa reference hote hain: koi /proc/PID/ns/net open rakhe (nsenter, monitoring agent), ya bind-mount kare (ip netns add). Tab INIT mar jaata hai, container khatam, lekin namespace zinda -- aur saath mein host par mbx... interface bhi. Plus, namespace destruction asynchronous hai (kernel workqueue), toh 'minibox return hua' ka matlab 'interface gaya' guarantee nahi.

Isliye cleanup() pehle network.remove_host_side() chalata hai (ENODEV = pehle hi gaya, theek). Naya test test_host_end_is_deleted_even_if_something_keeps_the_namespace_alive INIT ka PID cgroup.procs se leta hai, uska /proc/PID/ns/net open rakhta hai, container ko khatam karta hai, aur check karta hai ki host end gaya. Ab N5 3 mein se 3 runs red. Cleanup failure bhi guarded hai: delete fail ho toh warning, lekin cgroup aur state dir cleanup chalta rahe.
why_needed: Cleanup ko 'kernel kar dega' par chhodna tab tak theek hai jab tak koi aur reference na pakde; production mein hamesha koi pakadta hai.
real_world_analogy: Kiraye ka ghar: kiraayedaar chala gaya toh maalik maan leta hai ghar khaali. Lekin kisi ke paas doosri chaabi hai (open fd) -- ghar 'khaali' nahi hua. Apna saamaan khud uthao.
how_it_works: Network namespace ek refcounted kernel object hai (struct net). Process, open nsfs fd, aur bind mount teeno refcount badhate hain. Last ref jaane par cleanup_net workqueue devices unregister karta hai.
in_this_project: container.cleanup(link=...) aur network.remove_host_side(); test ne N5 ko catchable banaya.

# real, tests/integration/test_network.py (trimmed)

    net = wait_net_json(box.state_dir, "netpin", p)

advantages: External tools ke saath bhi leak nahi
disadvantages: Ek extra netlink call har exit par
SIGKILL ke baad (minibox khud mare) phir bhi leak
common_mistakes: Kernel ke implicit cleanup par bharosa
Mutation pakda nahi gaya toh code ko bekaar maan lena -- test kamzor tha
Cleanup mein ek failure se baaki cleanup skip
follow_up_questions: Namespace pinned ho toh container ka eth0 kahan rehta hai?
minibox SIGKILL ho toh leftovers kaise gc karoge?
ip netns kaise namespace ko naam deta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Explicit cleanup (deterministic, ek call) vs implicit (zero code, lekin refcount aur async timing par nirbhar). Explicit choose kiya; ENODEV ko success maana taaki dono raste safe.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Namespace pinned: host end leak (N5 test). minibox SIGKILL: koi cleanup nahi (README NOT implemented). Delete EPERM jaisa error: warning, baaki cleanup jaari.
advanced.alternatives: Host end ko bhi container namespace mein... nahi ho sakta; ya interfaces ko ek naam prefix se gc command se saaf karna (minibox gc, jo nahi hai).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Leak har container par ek interface -- 1000s leaks routing table aur memory bhar dete; gc zaroori ho jaata.
advanced.production_improvements: Startup par stale mbx* links ka gc (jinka koi cgroup nahi); state ko kernel ke saath reconcile karna (docker daemon yahi karta hai restart par).

question: With `--net veth`, what exactly can the container reach, and why was NAT and a default route left out on purpose?
answer_hinglish:
Container ke paas ek hi route hai: connected 10.200.N.0/30 dev eth0. Default route nahi. Iska matlab: host end (10.200.N.1) ke alawa kisi bhi address par packet bhejo toh kernel turant 'Network unreachable' deta hai -- packet container se nikalta hi nahi. Test 192.0.2.1 (documentation address) se yahi check karta hai.

Host tak kya pahunchta hai, woh host ki INPUT chain decide karti hai (container ke packets host ke liye local delivery hain). A2 par INPUT ICMP accept karta hai aur naye TCP sirf 22/80/443 par -- toh container host ko ping kar sakta hai, lekin host ki baaki services par naya TCP reject. Host container ko TCP khol sakta hai (reply ESTABLISHED hai) -- test nc se connect karta hai. Do containers alag /30 mein hain, unke beech route nahi -- test check karta hai ki ek doosre ko ping nahi kar sakte.

NAT kyun nahi: internet access ke liye default route + host par forwarding + MASQUERADE chahiye. A2 par FORWARD chain aur nat table Docker manage karta hai; unme rules daalna shared server par risk tha. Default route ke bina packet FORWARD tak pahunchta hi nahi, toh koi iptables rule nahi -- before/after snapshot mein filter aur nat tables identical. Yaad rakho: minibox security boundary nahi hai (root, capabilities sab); network isolation sirf honest programs ke liye hai.
why_needed: Interview mein 'container kya reach kar sakta hai' ka jawab routes + firewall + namespaces teeno se aata hai, sirf ek se nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek kamra jiska sirf ek darwaza hai, aur woh darwaza sirf reception (host) mein khulta hai. Reception ke guard (INPUT rules) decide karte hain ki aap kahan jaa sakte ho. Building se bahar ka raasta (NAT) banaya hi nahi.
how_it_works: Routing decision pehle hota hai: no route -> ENETUNREACH sendto() par hi. Host ke liye destined packet INPUT chain se jaata hai; dusron ke liye FORWARD (yahan kabhi nahi). ip_forward=1 hone se bhi farq nahi padta jab tak container ke paas route na ho.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_network.py
def test_nothing_beyond_the_host_end_is_routable(box):
    # 192.0.2.1 is TEST-NET-1 (documentation only). With no default route the kernel refuses at once:
    # no packet leaves the container, so there is nothing for the host to forward or NAT.
    r = box.run("ping -c 1 -W 1 192.0.2.1 2>&1; echo rc=$?", "--net", "veth")
    assert "Network unreachable" in r.stdout and "rc=0" not in r.stdout, r.stdout
disadvantages: Internet nahi, DNS nahi
Host ki INPUT policy par nirbhar (doosre host par behaviour alag)
common_mistakes: Sochna ki namespace = firewall
Default route daal kar maan lena ki FORWARD DROP bacha lega
Host ke INPUT rules ko ignore karna
follow_up_questions: Container root hai; kya woh khud default route add karke bahar jaa sakta hai?
Host ki services ko container se kaise bachaoge?
Port publishing bina NAT ke kaise?

question: Design stage 4b for minibox: give containers internet access and published ports the way docker does. What would you add, and how would you run it safely?
answer_hinglish:
Docker ka default bridge network ka recipe:
(1) Ek bridge interface (minibox ke liye mbx0) jisme host ends ports ki tarah lagte hain; containers /30 ki jagah ek /24 share karte hain (bridge ka address gateway, jaise 10.200.0.1/24).
(2) Container mein default route via gateway, aur /etc/resolv.conf (host ka ya ek public resolver).
(3) Host par forwarding (ip_forward=1) aur FORWARD accept rules: bridge se bahar, aur bahar se bridge ke liye sirf RELATED,ESTABLISHED.
(4) NAT: iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.200.0.0/24 ! -o mbx0 -j MASQUERADE -- private source ko host ke address se badlo, conntrack reply ko wapas map karta hai.
(5) Port publishing -p 8080:80: nat PREROUTING (bahar se) aur OUTPUT (host se hi) mein DNAT host:8080 -> container:80, aur FORWARD mein us flow ka accept.

Safety: A2 par Docker FORWARD aur nat ka owner hai (FORWARD -> DOCKER-USER -> DOCKER-FORWARD -> REJECT). Apne rules DOCKER-USER mein ya ek apni chain mein jo DOCKER-USER se jump ho; har rule par comment tag (minibox); kabhi save nahi; cleanup tag se; before/after iptables-save diff. Behtar: ek throwaway VM ya bina Docker wala server -- PLAN.md yahi recommend karta hai aur isi wajah se 4b nahi kiya.

Tests: container se host ke bahar ek controlled endpoint (doosra private server) tak pahunchna, MASQUERADE se source IP host ka dikhna (endpoint par log), DNAT se published port, aur cleanup ke baad rules zero.
why_needed: Senior interviews mein 'docker network andar se kaise kaam karta hai' design karke batana common hai.
real_world_analogy: Building (host) ke andar ek corridor (bridge) jisme saare kamre khulte hain; bahar jaane wale har letter par building ka address (MASQUERADE); aur reception par ek board 'flat 80 ke liye gate 8080' (DNAT).
how_it_works: Bridge L2 switch hai; MASQUERADE SNAT ka dynamic form (outgoing interface ka address); conntrack har flow ka mapping yaad rakhta hai taaki reply un-NAT ho. DNAT PREROUTING mein routing decision se pehle hota hai.
in_this_project: Abhi minibox sirf step 0 karta hai (veth, /30, no route). PLAN.md 'Stage 4 decision' mein 4b ka plan aur na karne ki wajah likhi hai.
code_example:
# plan only (not implemented) -- the rules stage 4b would add, from PLAN.md
ip link add mbx0 type bridge && ip addr add 10.200.0.1/24 dev mbx0 && ip link set mbx0 up
ip link set mbxXXXXXXXX master mbx0                  # each host end becomes a bridge port
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.200.0.0/24 ! -o mbx0 -m comment --comment minibox -j MASQUERADE
iptables -I DOCKER-USER -i mbx0 ! -o mbx0 -m comment --comment minibox -j ACCEPT
iptables -I DOCKER-USER -o mbx0 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -m comment --comment minibox -j ACCEPT
advantages: Containers ek doosre se baat kar sakte (same bridge)
disadvantages: Host firewall mein rules = shared state
Containers ek doosre ko reach kar sakte (isolation kam)
conntrack table ek aur resource
common_mistakes: Docker ki chains ke beech random jagah rules daalna
Rules save kar dena (reboot ke baad bhi)
OUTPUT chain DNAT bhool jaana (host se localhost:8080 kaam nahi karega)
follow_up_questions: nftables mein yeh kaise likhoge?
Rootless containers (slirp4netns/pasta) bina root ke network kaise dete hain?
Inter-container isolation bridge par kaise wapas laoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Bridge + NAT: full connectivity, lekin host firewall mein shared state. Veth-only: zero host changes, lekin sirf host tak. Routed (no NAT, host routes per container): no NAT cost, lekin upstream ko routes chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Docker restart apni chains flush karke rebuild kare: hamare rules chale jaate (ya order badal jaata). MASQUERADE galat interface par: host ka hi traffic NAT. Rules leak: cleanup crash.
advanced.alternatives: macvlan/ipvlan (container ko LAN par seedha address), routed /32 per container (Calico style), user-space networking (slirp4netns, pasta) rootless ke liye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Hazaron containers: iptables rules linear -- nftables sets ya eBPF (Cilium) chahiye; conntrack table size tune; /24 se bada pool.
advanced.production_improvements: Ek apni chain (MINIBOX-FWD) jisme ek jump; nftables table jo atomically add/remove ho; cleanup tag se idempotent; startup reconcile.

question: Two of the new network tests failed on the first run on the server. How would you debug a container's network from the host, and what was the actual cause here?
answer_hinglish:
Pehli run mein 9 mein se 2 fail hue. Error padha: `cat: can't open '/sys/class/net/eth0/operstate': No such file or directory` aur `ls: /sys/class/net: No such file or directory`. Wahi output mein `ip addr` dikha raha tha `eth0@if6: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>` aur `inet 10.200.0.2/30` -- yaani feature sahi tha, TEST galat tha. Wajah: minibox container mein sirf /proc aur ek minimal /dev mount karta hai, /sys nahi (README ka 'NOT a security boundary' section bhi yahi kehta hai). Fix: tests ko /proc/net/dev aur `ip link` par shift kiya -- feature ko nahi chhua.

General debugging toolkit host se: (1) net.json (minibox ka 'inspect') se interface naam aur addresses; (2) `ip -br link` host par mbx* end, uska state, aur `@ifN` se peer ka index; (3) container ke namespace mein ghuso: `nsenter -t <INIT ka host PID> -n ip addr` / `ip route` -- PID cgroup.procs se; (4) `ping` host end se container IP, aur `tcpdump -i mbxXXXX` dekho packet nikal raha hai ya nahi; (5) firewall: `iptables -S INPUT` aur counters (`-v`). Order: link up? address? route? firewall? -- neeche se upar.

Lesson: test fail ho toh pehle poora output padho; yahan stdout ne khud bata diya ki interface UP hai.
why_needed: Network bugs 'kuch nahi chal raha' jaise dikhte hain; layer by layer check karna hi fast tareeka hai.
real_world_analogy: Bijli nahi aa rahi: pehle check karo bulb (test) kharab hai ya wiring (feature). Yahan bulb ka socket (/sys) hi nahi tha, wiring theek thi.
how_it_works: nsenter -n setns(CLONE_NEWNET) karke command chalata hai: host ke binaries, container ka network stack. Isliye container image mein ip na ho tab bhi debug ho jaata hai.
in_this_project: SERVER_RUN.md section 6 mein first run (7 passed, 2 failed) aur fix likha hai; test_veth_adds_exactly_one_interface ab /proc/net/dev padhta hai.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_network.py (after the fix)
def test_veth_adds_exactly_one_interface(box):
    # the default (loopback only) is test_isolation.test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up
    r = box.run("tail -n +3 /proc/net/dev | cut -d: -f1 | tr -d ' '", "--net", "veth")
    assert r.returncode == 0 and sorted(r.stdout.split()) == ["eth0", "lo"], (r.stdout, r.stderr)
advantages: nsenter se container image par dependency nahi
disadvantages: nsenter ke liye root aur host PID chahiye
tcpdump host par install hona chahiye
common_mistakes: Test fail = feature broken maan lena
Container ke andar ke tools par bharosa (image mein ho hi na)
Firewall ko sabse pehle blame karna
follow_up_questions: @if6 ka matlab kya hai?
Container ke andar /sys kaise mount karoge, aur risk kya hai?
tcpdump se ARP problem kaise pehchanoge?

question: Write a function that encodes one netlink attribute (rtattr) and a parser that splits a buffer of attributes, and show a test that would catch a padding bug.
answer_hinglish:
Requirement: attr(type, payload) -> bytes: header = struct '=HH' (length, type), length = 4 + len(payload) (padding ke bina), phir payload, phir zero bytes jab tak total 4 ka multiple na ho. Parser: offset 0 se, header padho, length < 4 ya buffer ke bahar jaaye toh error (malformed input par chup-chaap galat parse se behtar), payload = data[off+4 : off+length], type ke upar ke 2 flag bits mask karo (0x3FFF), agla offset = align4(length).

align4(n) = (n + 3) & ~3 -- bit trick: 3 jodo, neeche ke 2 bits saaf karo.

Test jo padding bug pakde: expected bytes HAATH se likho, encoder se nahi. 'eth0\0' (5 bytes) ka attribute = 09 00 03 00 'eth0' 00 + 3 padding = 12 bytes. Aur ek already-aligned case ('veth', 4 bytes -> length 8, padding 0) taaki over-padding bhi pakda jaaye. Round-trip test (encode phir parse) akela kaafi nahi: agar encoder aur parser dono same galti karein (dono padding bhool jaayein), round-trip pass ho jaayega. minibox ke mutation N10 (padding hatao) ne 13 tests red kiye -- hand-written bytes wale unit tests aur kernel dono ne pakda.
why_needed: Binary protocols ke encoders interviews mein common coding exercise hain, aur 'test ko independent oracle chahiye' woh baat hai jo log miss karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Form bharte waqt har field ek fixed-size box mein: agar aap box chhota kar do toh agla field galat box mein jaayega, aur padhne wala galat padhega.
how_it_works: struct '=' native byte order bina native alignment ke; netlink host byte order use karta hai. Python slicing ke saath zero-copy nahi, lekin chhote messages ke liye theek.
in_this_project: minibox/rtnetlink.py mein attr(), parse_attrs(), align4(); tests/unit/test_rtnetlink.py mein hand-written bytes.
disadvantages: Nested attributes ke liye recursion caller ko karni padti hai
Duplicate types ki list (dict nahi) -- caller decide kare
common_mistakes: Length mein padding jodna
Round-trip test ko hi proof maan lena
Malformed length par infinite loop (length 0)
follow_up_questions: length 0 wala attribute aaye toh tumhara parser kya karega?
Nested attribute ko recursively kaise parse karoge?
Isko generic TLV library kaise banaoge?

question: Why did minibox talk rtnetlink by hand instead of running `ip link add ...` with subprocess or using a library like pyroute2?
answer_hinglish:
Teen options the:
(A) subprocess se `ip link add mbx.. type veth peer name eth0 netns PID`, `ip addr add`, `ip link set up` -- sabse kam code, battle-tested.
(B) pyroute2 -- full netlink library.
(C) khud rtnetlink messages banana (stdlib socket).

minibox ne C choose kiya, teen wajah se: (1) Project ka rule: zero third-party runtime dependencies (pyroute2 out); aur PLAN.md ka principle 'every syscall visible' -- mount/pivot_root ke liye bhi ctypes isi wajah se. Learning project mein netlink ka format khud likhna hi seekhne ka point hai. (2) iproute2 host par hona chahiye (A option) -- usually hota hai, lekin ek external binary ka output/exit code parse karna aur uske versions ka behaviour ek aur dependency hai. (3) Errors: netlink ACK se seedha errno milta hai (EEXIST, ENODEV), jo code mein typed handle hota hai (delete_link missing_ok).

Cost honestly: ~230 lines, binary encoding ki galtiyan silent ho sakti hain -- isliye hand-written byte tests aur 11 mutation checks (N9: ACK error ignore, N10: padding) aur A2 par asli kernel. Kernel ke extended error messages (extack) parse nahi kiye, toh error sirf errno string hai. Production mein main (B) ya Go ka vishvananda/netlink use karta, jaisa runc/CNI karte hain.
why_needed: Har design decision ka 'kyun' aur 'kis keemat par' batana senior signal hai, khaas kar jab tumne kam popular raasta chuna.
real_world_analogy: Khana khud banana (C) vs restaurant (A) vs meal kit (B): seekhna hai toh khud banao, lekin recipe test karo; roz ke liye restaurant theek.
how_it_works: Teeno same kernel API tak pahunchte hain; fark hai ki encoding kaun karta hai aur errors kaise aate hain. subprocess har call par fork+exec (~ms) karta hai; netlink socket ek baar khula, requests microseconds mein.
in_this_project: minibox/rtnetlink.py ka module docstring aur PLAN.md ka decision 'veth over rtnetlink with a stdlib socket, not by running ip'.
disadvantages: Zyada code, binary bugs ka risk
extack messages nahi
Kam features (sirf jo chahiye)
common_mistakes: subprocess output ko string match karke errors pehchanna
Library choose karna bina dekhe ki woh kya dependencies laati hai
Khud likhna lekin independent tests na likhna
follow_up_questions: extack parse karke behtar error messages kaise doge?
Kab tum subprocess wala raasta prefer karoge?
Go mein yeh code kaisa dikhta?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hand-written (control + learning, risk binary bugs) vs library (features, dependency) vs CLI (simple, process + parsing overhead). Project ke rules ne C chuna; tests ne risk cover kiya.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat encoding: kernel EINVAL ya galat parse (N10). ACK error ignore: setup 'success' lekin interface nahi (N9). Reply buffer chhota: dump truncated (65536 abhi kaafi).
advanced.alternatives: pyroute2 (Python), vishvananda/netlink (Go, runc/CNI), libnl (C), ya CNI plugins ko exec karna (bridge, host-local) jaisa containerd karta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Netlink socket reuse se per-container cost kam; bahut containers par dump size badhta -- filtered dumps ya address cache.
advanced.production_improvements: extack parsing, NLM_F_ACK_TLVS, ek CNI-style plugin interface taaki networking runtime se alag ho.
